cards.text: Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, is writing to the believers in Rome. He's been warning the Gentiles there not to brag over Israel, and now he wants them to know a mystery so they won't be conceited. Friend, when Paul says 'mystery,' I lean in closer than a baker to a warm oven.

cards.question: Paul's mystery is about Israel. What has come to Israel in part?

cards.text: 'In part,' and with an 'until' on it? Friend, that's a snooze button, not an off switch.

cards.question: Paul says the hardening on Israel lasts until the full number of the ___ has come in.
Then Paul makes a big statement about Israel. What is it?

cards.text: Paul backs it up, 'as it is written': 'The Deliverer will come from Zion.' He brings receipts, friend, and not the faded kind I slept on for years in that junk drawer.

cards.question: In the Scripture Paul quotes, what will the Deliverer remove from Jacob?
In that same Scripture, God says His covenant with them is when He takes away their sins.

cards.text: Now Paul shows Israel from two sides. When it comes to the gospel, he tells the Gentiles, they're enemies on your account.

cards.question: But when it comes to election, Paul says Israel is loved. On account of whom?
Paul says God takes back His gifts and His call when people turn away from Him.

cards.text: Paul says it straight: 'For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.' The expired coupon I shared that drawer with only WISHED it could say that.
Paul's still talking to the Gentiles in Rome. He reminds them they used to disobey God, but now they've received mercy.

cards.question: How does Paul say the Gentiles in Rome received that mercy?
Now Israel has disobeyed too. Why, according to Paul?

answers.text: So they too may receive mercy
So God can choose someone else
So the Gentiles can replace them

cards.question: Paul sums it up: God has consigned everyone to ___ so that He may have ___ on everyone.

cards.text: Everyone. Gentiles, Israel and one dusty stamper from the back of a junk drawer, nobody in this line gets to say 'Not me.'
Eleven chapters of explaining, and now Paul just bursts out: 'O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God!' ELEVEN chapters, friend, and the man lands on 'O!' I respect it.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who studies hard enough can trace out all of God's ways.

cards.text: Then Paul pulls in Scripture with two questions: 'Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?'

cards.question: Paul asks who has known the mind of the Lord or been His counselor. What answer is he expecting?
Next Paul asks, 'Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?' What's his point?

answers.text: God keeps track of every gift

cards.text: Me, sending God a bill for my baking? He's the One who pulled me out of the drawer, friend, so I'm the one who owes HIM the cookies.
Then Paul ties it all together: 'For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things.'

cards.question: So who does Paul say gets the glory forever?

cards.text: 'To Him be the glory forever! Amen.' Friend, that's not a man finishing a chapter, that's a man who just ran out of room for anything but praise.

findings.problem: The opening card states two facts from outside the passage without a reference: Paul calls himself the apostle to the Gentiles (Romans 11:13), and he has been warning the Gentiles not to brag over Israel (Romans 11:18). The card cites only Romans 11:25.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Card 3 says the hardening is 'a snooze button, not an off switch.' This tells the baker the hardening is temporary, so it rules out the wrong answer 'Israel will stay hardened' on card 5.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke that restates Romans 11:32, which card 4 already covered. It does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: the outburst with the quote, 'ELEVEN chapters, friend, and the man lands on 'O!'' and 'I respect it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about Romans 11:35, which card 10 already quoted and asked about. It adds no part of the passage and does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Saying Paul is 'a man who just ran out of room for anything but praise' states Paul's inner state as fact. It is not marked as Papa Dorin's own guess.

rule.text: Feelings. He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.
